title.narrative: Local Physical and Land Use Development Plan (LPLDP) for Kilifi Municipality

description.narrative:
The project aims to develop a Local Physical and Land Use Development Plan (LPLDP) for Kilifi Municipality. The plan is envisaged to facilitate the development of a robust and balanced settlements in Kilifi Municipality that leverages the agricultural, industrial and tourism potential and provides supporting infrastructure while ensuring environmental protection. The Kilifi Municipality LPLDP is a response to the existing gap of lack of spatial framework for the municipality to guide a coordinated urban growth and development. The current existing plan for the town is outdated, and unable to respond to the existing urban growth demands and needs for protection of the fragile environment for the municipality. Due to the current dynamism in urbanization in the coastal towns coupled with the impetus brought about by devolution, the revised legislative framework guiding planning and urban management, it is imperative for the municipality as matter of priority to prepare a spatial framework to guide the future urban growth in a secure, inclusive, and sustainable manner.
This LPLDP for Kilifi Municipality project is anchored on the Go Blue Result Area 2 – Connecting People, Cities and Ocean: Innovative Land Sea Planning and Management for sustainable and resilient Kenya Coast which is a partnership between the EU and the Government of Kenya to advance the Blue Economy Agenda through Coastal Development. The Go Blue project is a four-year project funded by the EU to unlock the potential of land-sea opportunities in coastal urban centers for sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth with employment impact, while conserving and sustainably using the coastal and marine environment as well as promoting effective and integrated maritime governance.
The Go Blue project is a catalytic programme which has triggered other activities and investment. The need for the Kilifi LPLDP was identified at the inception phase of the Go Blue project and it is therefore an additional component and significantly contributing to the larger Go Blue project, especially the ongoing planning work in Kilifi County. In Kilifi, the Go Blue project endeavors to support the implementation of the neighborhood and Coastal zone management plan for Kilifi Creek to address the complexity for Land-sea eco system preservation linked with blue economy potential, and the design, develop and enhanced the functionality of an urban coastal public space – Mazingira Park situated within the Kilifi Creek into a sustainable, safe and accessible public space through the preparation of a neighbourhood plan that demonstrates sustainable and integrated land-sea planning approaches and upholds cultural heritage.; support the establishment of Data Center and GIS LAB that will be used in natural resource mapping as well as urban planning and development control within the County; training course on data, information management and planning for key technical staff.
UN-Habitat will adopt a participatory planning approach involving communities and all relevant stakeholders to ensure an inclusive and context relevant plan. The process will include site surveys, stakeholder workshops and meetings and capacity building activities for the members of the local government and civil society throughout the planning process.
The project’s expected outcomes include improved delivery of urban basic services and amenities in Kilifi Municipality; improved planning and investment in infrastructure development in Kilifi Municipality; improved land use and development management in Kilifi Municipality; and improved Local Economic Development.
